title: Impact Of The Gut Microbiota On Host Cells Energy Metabolism in Health And In Inflammatory Bowel
official: Impact Of The Gut Microbiota On Host Cells Energy Metabolism in Health And In Inflammatory Bowel Disease (ENERGISED-Clinic)
summary: Main objective: Evaluate the impact of the gut microbiota, and of its alteration in inflammatory bowel disease, on peripheral immune cells energy metabolism.
conditions:
Healthy volunteers : 
Healthy adults with no history of gastrointestinal disease

Patients with IBD in remission
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. For volunteers: Age ≥ 18 ans et < 50 ans avec IMC compris entre 17 et 25 km/m²
2. Patients with IBD: Regular bowel movement defined as at least 1 stool every other day and maximum 3 stools per day
3. Patients with IBD: Patient with health insurance (AME except)
4. Patients with IBD: Informed Written consent
5. For volunteers: For women, female of child-bearing age with an active contraception (hormonal, intrauterine device, bilateral tubal occlusion, sexual abstinence*) and this during at least the period of treatment (up to v2)
6. For volunteers: Regular bowel movement defined as at least 1 stool every other day and maximum 3 stools per day
7. For volunteerss: -	Patient with health insurance (AME except)
8. For volunteers: Informed Written consent
9. Patients with IBD: Age ≥ 18 ans et < 50 ans avec IMC compris entre 17 et 25 kg/m²
10. Patients with IBD: Crohn’s Disease (Excepting disease involving only the upper GI tract) or ulcerative colitis (excepting disease involving only the rectum), according to the Lennard-Jones criteria for at least 6 months (15 patients with Crohn’s disease and 15 with ulcerative colitis will be recruited)
11. Patients with IBD: Patient in steroid-free clinical remission for at least 6 months (for Crohn’s disease: CDAI <150 the week before inclusion, for ulcerative colitis: Partial Mayo Clinic score of 0 or 1).
12. Patients with IBD: Female of child-bearing age with an active contraception. Efficient contraception  include oral contraception, intrauterine devices hormonal device, intrauterine hormone-releasing system, sterilization method and other forms of contraception with failure rate <1%)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Healthy volunteers: Significant chronic disease and particularly chronic gastrointestinal diseases, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, renal alteration or history of abdominal surgery (except appendectomy).
2. Patients with IBD: Diagnosis of Crohn’s disease restricted to the upper gastrointestinal tract (oesophagus, stomac, duodenum, jejunum)
3. Patients with IBD: Current stoma (Ileostomy or a colostomy) or stoma in the last 6 months or any other intra-abdominal surgery within 3 months prior to inclusion
4. Healthy volunteers: Curative long-term treatment
5. Patients with IBD: Participation in any other interventional study
6. Patients with IBD: Patients under legal protection
7. Patient with IBD: Diagnosis of ulcerative colitis restricted to the rectum
8. Healthy volunteers : Pregnant or breastfeeding women
9. Healthy volunteers : blood donation in the 3 months before the study
10. Healthy volunteers: Taking antibiotic or antifungal (oral) in the previous 3 months before planned day 0 (V1)
11. Healthy volunteers : probiotics in the month preceding day 0 (V1)
12. Healthy voluteers: contra-indications to the administration of gentamicin (refer to SmPC)
13. Healthy volunteers: consumption of a low-calorie diet or any other special diet (except vegetarian) in the month before day 0
14. Healthy volunteers: abdominal surgery in the past (except for appendectomy)
15. Healthy volunteers: allergy against the antibiotics and antifungal treatment used in this study or to their excipients
16. Healthy volunteers: fructose intolerance
17. Patient with IBD: Fructose intolerance
18. Healthy volunteers: Participation in any other interventional study
19. Healthy volunteers: under legal protection
20. Patients with IBD: Pregnant or breastfeeding women
21. Patients with IBD: blood donation in the 3 months before the study
22. Patients with IBD: Taking antibiotic or antifungal (oral) in the previous 3 months before planned day 0
23. Patients with IBD: probiotics in the month preceding day 0 and during the study
24. Patients with IBD: Ileal resection > 50cm or colectomy
